q1: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2: SELECT PROJECT.PROJECT_ID, IFNULL(ROUND(AVG(EMPLOYEE.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2), 0) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT LEFT JOIN EMPLOYEE ON PROJECT.EMPLOYEE_ID = EMPLOYEE.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY PROJECT.PROJECT_ID

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 uses an INNER JOIN, which means only projects that have matching employees in the EMPLOYEE table will appear in the result. Q2 uses a LEFT JOIN, which means all projects will appear, and if there is no matching employee, AVG will return NULL (but IFNULL converts it to 0). The difference arises when a project has no matching employee in the EMPLOYEE table.
counterexample_dsp: A project exists without a matching employee in the EMPLOYEE table. Q1 will not return this project, while Q2 will return it with an average of 0.
